name: Valletta Salt Pans
caption: Ancient salt pans glow copper at dusk — a working tradition unchanged for centuries.
description: These terraced salt pans have been harvested since the Bronze Age. Watch as local workers rake the crystalline salt into mounds that catch the light like scattered diamonds. Best visited during golden hour when the entire landscape transforms into warm amber tones.

name: Azure Window Ruins
caption: Where limestone cliffs meet endless Mediterranean blue.
description: Though the famous arch collapsed in 2017, this stretch of coastline remains one of the most dramatic viewpoints along the entire coastal arc. The sheer limestone faces drop directly into turquoise waters below.

name: Fisherman's Cove
caption: Colorful boats bob in a harbor time forgot.
description: This tiny fishing village has resisted modernization for generations. Pull up a chair at any waterfront trattoria and order the day's catch — likely grilled on the spot with nothing but lemon, olive oil, and sea salt.

name: Lighthouse Point
caption: A sentinel watching over endless waves.
description: Climb the 142 steps to the top of this 19th-century lighthouse for sweeping 360-degree views. On clear days, you can see across to the distant mainland. The keeper's cottage now serves espresso and pastries.

name: Sea Cave Cathedral
caption: Natural acoustics amplify the whisper of waves.
description: Accessible only by small boat or a steep cliff path, this sea cave features natural openings in its ceiling that create ethereal light beams throughout the day. The water inside is impossibly clear and cool.

name: Cliffside Chapel
caption: Faith carved into the edge of the world.
description: This tiny stone chapel has watched over sailors for over 400 years. Light a candle inside and take a moment of silence. The simple bell tower rings only on Sundays and major feast days.

name: Olive Grove Terrace
caption: Centuries-old trees still bearing fruit.
description: The fourth generation of this family tends groves planted by their great-grandparents. Sample cold-pressed oils aged in terracotta amphorae, paired with fresh bread baked in wood-fired ovens.

name: Hill Town Belltower
caption: A town frozen in medieval time.
description: Wander cobblestone alleys where laundry still hangs between buildings and nonnas watch from shuttered windows. The campanile offers the best vantage point over terracotta rooftops stretching to distant hills.

name: Monastery Ruins
caption: Stone arches framing sky and silence.
description: Founded in the 12th century, this monastery was abandoned during the great plague. Today, wildflowers grow through cracked flagstones and swallows nest in vaulted ceilings. Entry is free; donations maintain the grounds.

name: Vineyard Overlook
caption: Rows of vines marching toward forever.
description: This boutique winery produces fewer than 3,000 bottles annually using indigenous grape varieties. Book the sunset tasting on their terrace overlooking the entire valley — reservations essential.

name: Stone Bridge Village
caption: Roman engineering still serving shepherds today.
description: This humpback bridge has carried foot traffic, donkeys, and now tourists across the same river for nearly two millennia. The adjacent cafe serves traditional shepherd's pie using recipes unchanged for generations.

name: Hermit's Cave Chapel
caption: A sanctuary carved by faithful hands.
description: A moderate 20-minute hike leads to this chapel hollowed directly into limestone cliffs. Frescoes from the 14th century still cling to interior walls. Bring water and wear proper shoes.

name: Riverside Mill
caption: Water wheels still turning after 300 years.
description: This fully restored grain mill demonstrates traditional milling techniques every weekend. Purchase freshly ground flour or try the mill's signature honey cake made from a secret family recipe.

name: Gorge Walkway
caption: Carved by water, walked by wonder.
description: A wooden boardwalk clings to the side of this dramatic gorge, leading past three waterfalls and through tunnels blasted into rock. The final viewpoint overlooks the entire canyon system.

name: Market Square
caption: Saturday mornings smell of basil and bread.
description: Every Saturday, farmers from surrounding valleys bring heirloom tomatoes, artisan cheeses, and cured meats to this shaded piazza. Come hungry and bring a tote bag for your treasures.

name: Floodlit Fortress
caption: Stone walls holding centuries of stories.
description: This hilltop fortress commands views across three valleys. Evening visits reveal dramatic floodlighting that brings ancient battlements to life. The onsite museum houses artifacts from Roman through Napoleonic eras.

name: Thermal Springs
caption: Mineral-rich waters soothing body and soul.
description: These naturally heated springs have attracted bathers since Roman times. Multiple pools range from warm to hot, each with different mineral compositions. Towel rental available; modest swimwear required.

name: River Bend Café
caption: Espresso and almond croissants by the water.
description: Family-owned since 1952, this riverside café is famous for its cannoli and strong coffee. Outdoor tables sit under plane trees right at the water's edge. Perfect mid-journey rest stop.
